claim: Endometriosis is a heterogenous disease with likely multiple pathogeneses and as-yet-undefined subtypes.
source: As a heterogenous disease with likely multiple pathogeneses and as-yet-undefined subtypes, progress in endometriosis treatment is currently limited by a lack of appropriate models and cohorts for research.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of endometriosis in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Almost half of all publicly available datasets labelled as 'endometriosis' do not represent true disease as they are based on eutopic endometrium.
source: Almost half of all publicly available datasets labelled as 'endometriosis' do not represent true disease as they are based on eutopic endometrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data analysis presented in the manuscript showing 59/122 (48.37%) of datasets contained no representation of true endometriotic disease.

claim: Eutopic endometrial cells and tissues are frequently being used to represent endometriotic lesions, despite the unequivocal differences at both the tissue and cellular levels.
source: Eutopic endometrial cells and tissues are frequently being used to represent endometriotic lesions, despite the unequivocal differences at both the tissue and cellular levels.
evidence: This is supported by the dataset analysis and the review of biological differences between endometrium and endometriosis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Endometriosis is a heterogenous disease with multiple proposed pathogeneses.
source: Despite being a heterogenous disease with multiple proposed pathogeneses (Signorile et al., 2022) and as-yet-undefined subtypes, the majority of preclinical research in endometriosis remains focused on an endometrium-dependent aetiology.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Signorile et al., 2022.

claim: Endometriosis is 3.4 times more common than dementia according to conservative estimates from the World Health Organization.
source: Conservative estimates from the World Health Organization put endometriosis as 3.4 times more common than dementia (World Health Organization, 2023a; World Health Organization, 2023b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to World Health Organization reports from 2023.

claim: There are 37,384 research articles on endometriosis in total to date.
source: However, while there are 37,384 research articles on endometriosis in total to date, dementia had 34,546 articles published in 2023 and 2024 alone (https://www.webofscience.com term = endometriosis; term = dementia, accessed February 5, 2025).
evidence: This is based on a Web of Science search conducted on February 5, 2025.

claim: Dementia had 34,546 articles published in 2023 and 2024 alone.
source: However, while there are 37,384 research articles on endometriosis in total to date, dementia had 34,546 articles published in 2023 and 2024 alone (https://www.webofscience.com term = endometriosis; term = dementia, accessed February 5, 2025).
evidence: This is based on a Web of Science search conducted on February 5, 2025.

claim: Endometriosis was listed as one of nine conditions in women leading to the greatest personal, societal, and economic burden globally at the World Economic Forum in January 2025.
source: At the World Economic Forum in January 2025, endometriosis was listed as one of nine conditions in women leading to the greatest personal, societal, and economic burden globally (World Economic Forum, 2025).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Economic Forum, 2025.

claim: Lack of funding remains one of the most substantial barriers to obstetrics and gynaecology research.
source: Lack of funding remains one of the most substantial barriers to obstetrics and gynaecology research, which has consistently been one of the lowest funded NIH specialties in the last decade (Schlafly and Sebro, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Schlafly and Sebro, 2022.

claim: Obstetrics and gynaecology has consistently been one of the lowest funded NIH specialties in the last decade.
source: Lack of funding remains one of the most substantial barriers to obstetrics and gynaecology research, which has consistently been one of the lowest funded NIH specialties in the last decade (Schlafly and Sebro, 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Schlafly and Sebro, 2022.

claim: The NIH budget for endometriosis research is projected to double between 2020 and 2024.
source: This may be on the precipice of change, with the NIH budget for endometriosis research projected to double between 2020 and 2024 (National Institutes of Health, 2024), during which time there has been a marked increase in both overall and interdisciplinary clinical trials (Xu et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to National Institutes of Health, 2024.

claim: There has been a marked increase in both overall and interdisciplinary clinical trials in endometriosis between 2020 and 2024.
source: This may be on the precipice of change, with the NIH budget for endometriosis research projected to double between 2020 and 2024 (National Institutes of Health, 2024), during which time there has been a marked increase in both overall and interdisciplinary clinical trials (Xu et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2024.

claim: Endometriosis is defined as a chronic inflammatory disease marked by the presence of lesions in extrauterine locations which microscopically represent endometrium-like epithelium and/or stroma.
source: Endometriosis is defined as a chronic inflammatory disease marked by the presence of lesions in extrauterine locations which microscopically represent endometrium-like epithelium and/or stroma (Tomassetti et al., 2021).
evidence: This is the clinical definition of endometriosis supported by a citation to Tomassetti et al., 2021.

claim: Endometriosis lesions are cellularly heterogeneous, with significant contribution from endothelial, myeloid, and lymphocyte populations.
source: Endometriosis lesions are cellularly heterogeneous, with significant contribution from endothelial, myeloid, and lymphocyte populations (Tan et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tan et al., 2022.

claim: The most common classification system defines endometriosis phenotypes according to their macroscopic appearance during surgery, defined as superficial (<5 mm invasion of the peritoneum or serosa), deep infiltrating (>5 mm invasion), or ovarian cystic endometriomas.
source: The most common classification system defines phenotypes according to their macroscopic appearance during surgery, defined as superficial (<5 mm invasion of the peritoneum or serosa), deep infiltrating (>5 mm invasion), or ovarian cystic endometriomas.
evidence: This describes the standard classification system for endometriosis phenotypes.

claim: Endometriomas are highly enriched for stromal cells compared to peritoneal lesions.
source: While single-cell transcriptomic analysis of endometriotic lesions has revealed that endometriomas are highly enriched for stromal cells compared to peritoneal lesions (Fonseca et al., 2023), the sample sizes remain small, and cellular proportions are heterogenous between patients, even within the same phenotype (Tan et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fonseca et al., 2023.

claim: Both peritoneal lesions and endometriomas can share common somatic mutations, providing evidence for potential clonal development of disease from a common initiation in some patients.
source: Furthermore, investigations of intrapatient mutational signatures have demonstrated that both peritoneal lesions and endometriomas can share common somatic mutations, providing evidence for potential clonal development of disease from a common initiation in some patients (Praetorius et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Praetorius et al., 2022.

claim: Attempts to molecularly subtype endometriosis revealed distinct transcriptional signatures relating to fibrosis or immune dysfunction, which are independent of surgical phenotype.
source: Attempts to molecularly subtype endometriosis revealed distinct transcriptional signatures relating to fibrosis or immune dysfunction, which are independent of surgical phenotype (Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2023.

claim: 45/122 (36.89%) datasets contained eutopic endometrium only.
source: Most notably, 45/122 (36.89%) datasets contained eutopic endometrium only (Figure 2A), more than any other biospecimen type.
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: When combined with the endometrium samples, almost half of all biospecimens listed as 'endometriosis' had no representation of true endometriotic disease (59/122, 48.37%).
source: When combined with the endometrium samples, almost half of all biospecimens listed as 'endometriosis' had no representation of true endometriotic disease (59/122, 48.37%).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: There has been a steady increase in the overall number of datasets published each year.
source: When considering the year of publication, there has been a steady increase in the overall number of datasets published each year (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C of the manuscript.

claim: Annual representations of endometrium-only datasets are persistent at approximately 50%.
source: Despite this, annual representations of endometrium-only datasets are persistent at approximately 50%.
evidence: This is a finding from the temporal analysis of datasets shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There has been an increase in the number of endometriotic cell samples since 2012.
source: There has been an increase in the number of endometriotic cell samples since 2012, which have shown a trend towards immortalised cell lines since 2017.
evidence: This is a finding from the temporal analysis of datasets.

claim: All primary cells from endometriotic cell datasets were stromal (16/16, 100%).
source: For datasets containing endometriotic cells, one dataset contained endometriosis organoids of epithelial cell origin (1/17, 6.25%), while all primary cells were stromal (16/16, 100%).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis.

claim: All immortalised cell lines from endometriotic cell datasets were epithelial (13/13, 100%).
source: By contrast, all immortalised cell lines were epithelial (13/13, 100%).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis.

claim: Endometriomas were disproportionately represented, constituting 70.59% of primary cell samples and 72.22% of tissue datasets.
source: For datasets where phenotype was recorded, endometriomas were disproportionately represented, constituting 70.59% of primary cell samples and 72.22% of tissue datasets (endometrioma, multiple phenotypes containing endometrioma, Table 1), despite an overall prevalence of approximately 30% amongst endometriosis lesions (Bourdon et al., 2024).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis compared to the known prevalence cited from Bourdon et al., 2024.

claim: Endometriomas have an overall prevalence of approximately 30% amongst endometriosis lesions.
source: For datasets where phenotype was recorded, endometriomas were disproportionately represented, constituting 70.59% of primary cell samples and 72.22% of tissue datasets (endometrioma, multiple phenotypes containing endometrioma, Table 1), despite an overall prevalence of approximately 30% amongst endometriosis lesions (Bourdon et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bourdon et al., 2024.

claim: All endometriosis tissue datasets contained a biological control.
source: All endometriosis tissue datasets contained a biological control, while only 82% of primary cell experiments did (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Only 82% of primary cell experiments contained a biological control.
source: All endometriosis tissue datasets contained a biological control, while only 82% of primary cell experiments did (Table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: The majority of endometriosis tissue biospecimens were compared to eutopic endometrium as a biological control (13/36, 36.11%).
source: Of these controls, the majority of endometriosis tissue biospecimens were compared to eutopic endometrium as a biological control (13/36, 36.11%), while for three datasets, endometriosis lesions were compared to 'healthy' (non-endometriosis) endometrium only (3/36, 8.33%).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis.

claim: Adjacent tissues, representing the only microenvironment-relevant controls in the entire cohort, accounted for less than 5% of datasets analysed (6/122, 4.92%).
source: Collectively, these adjacent tissues, representing the only microenvironment-relevant controls in the entire cohort, accounted for less than 5% of datasets analysed (6/122, 4.92%).
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis.

claim: Deconvolution of cell populations has shown distinct cellular compositions of endometrial and endometriotic tissues, with epithelial cell populations significantly reduced in ectopic tissues when compared to eutopic, and the inverse true of stromal cells.
source: Deconvolution of cell populations has shown distinct cellular compositions of the two tissues, with epithelial cell populations significantly reduced in ectopic tissues when compared to eutopic, and the inverse true of stromal cells (Tan et al., 2022; Fonseca et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tan et al., 2022 and Fonseca et al., 2023.

claim: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased adherence compared to endometrial cells.
source: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased adherence (Delbandi et al., 2013), migration (Dai et al., 2019), and invasion (Kao et al., 2011) capacity compared to endometrial cells, owing to increased epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition (Zubrzycka et al., 2023) and decreased matrix metalloproteinase expression (Maoga et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Delbandi et al., 2013.

claim: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased migration compared to endometrial cells.
source: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased adherence (Delbandi et al., 2013), migration (Dai et al., 2019), and invasion (Kao et al., 2011) capacity compared to endometrial cells, owing to increased epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition (Zubrzycka et al., 2023) and decreased matrix metalloproteinase expression (Maoga et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dai et al., 2019.

claim: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased invasion capacity compared to endometrial cells.
source: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased adherence (Delbandi et al., 2013), migration (Dai et al., 2019), and invasion (Kao et al., 2011) capacity compared to endometrial cells, owing to increased epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition (Zubrzycka et al., 2023) and decreased matrix metalloproteinase expression (Maoga et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kao et al., 2011.

claim: Endometriotic cells show increased epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition compared to endometrial cells.
source: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased adherence (Delbandi et al., 2013), migration (Dai et al., 2019), and invasion (Kao et al., 2011) capacity compared to endometrial cells, owing to increased epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition (Zubrzycka et al., 2023) and decreased matrix metalloproteinase expression (Maoga et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zubrzycka et al., 2023.

claim: Endometriotic cells show decreased matrix metalloproteinase expression compared to endometrial cells.
source: Endometriotic cells demonstrate increased adherence (Delbandi et al., 2013), migration (Dai et al., 2019), and invasion (Kao et al., 2011) capacity compared to endometrial cells, owing to increased epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition (Zubrzycka et al., 2023) and decreased matrix metalloproteinase expression (Maoga et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Maoga et al., 2023.

claim: Transcriptional analysis has shown a coordinated pathway change in endometriotic tissue in favour of inflammatory activation, collagen formation, and extracellular matrix degradation.
source: Transcriptional analysis has shown a coordinated pathway change in endometriotic tissue in favour of inflammatory activation, collagen formation, and extracellular matrix degradation (Fonseca et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fonseca et al., 2023.

claim: Ectopic endometriotic cells are more proliferative both in vivo and in vitro compared to endometrial cells.
source: Ectopic endometriotic cells are also more proliferative both in vivo (Li et al., 1993) and in vitro (Wang et al., 2021), demonstrating a pro-survival phenotype of increased S-phase and decreased G0 cell cycle phase (Rashidi et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 1993 and Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Endometriosis cells demonstrate a pro-survival phenotype of increased S-phase and decreased G0 cell cycle phase.
source: Ectopic endometriotic cells are also more proliferative both in vivo (Li et al., 1993) and in vitro (Wang et al., 2021), demonstrating a pro-survival phenotype of increased S-phase and decreased G0 cell cycle phase (Rashidi et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rashidi et al., 2023.

claim: Upon cell death, endometriosis cells are more likely to undergo inflammatory modes including pyroptosis and ferroptosis.
source: Upon cell death, endometriosis cells are more likely to undergo inflammatory modes including pyroptosis (Xu et al., 2023) and ferroptosis (Li et al., 2021b; Zhang et al., 2022), instead of Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Caspase-3 mediated apoptosis (Delbandi et al., 2020) or autophagy (Huang et al., 2021) as is observed in eutopic endometrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2023, Li et al., 2021b, and Zhang et al., 2022.

claim: Eutopic endometrium cells undergo Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Caspase-3 mediated apoptosis or autophagy upon cell death.
source: Upon cell death, endometriosis cells are more likely to undergo inflammatory modes including pyroptosis (Xu et al., 2023) and ferroptosis (Li et al., 2021b; Zhang et al., 2022), instead of Bcl-2/Bcl-xL/Caspase-3 mediated apoptosis (Delbandi et al., 2020) or autophagy (Huang et al., 2021) as is observed in eutopic endometrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Delbandi et al., 2020 and Huang et al., 2021.

claim: Endometriotic lesions have higher levels of reactive oxygen species and hypoxia compared to matched endometrium.
source: At a tissue level, endometriotic lesions have higher levels of reactive oxygen species and hypoxia compared to matched endometrium (Dai et al., 2019; Yerlikaya et al., 2016), mediating both angiogenesis (Fu et al., 2018) and a metabolic reprogramming analogous to the Warburg effect (Kasvandik et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dai et al., 2019 and Yerlikaya et al., 2016.

claim: Higher levels of reactive oxygen species and hypoxia in endometriotic lesions mediate both angiogenesis and a metabolic reprogramming analogous to the Warburg effect.
source: At a tissue level, endometriotic lesions have higher levels of reactive oxygen species and hypoxia compared to matched endometrium (Dai et al., 2019; Yerlikaya et al., 2016), mediating both angiogenesis (Fu et al., 2018) and a metabolic reprogramming analogous to the Warburg effect (Kasvandik et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Fu et al., 2018, Kasvandik et al., 2016, and Chen et al., 2023.

claim: There is significantly increased immune cell infiltration in ectopic endometriosis tissues compared to eutopic endometrium.
source: There is significantly increased immune cell infiltration in ectopic endometriosis tissues (Tan et al., 2022) and acute dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immune function.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tan et al., 2022.

claim: Innate myeloid populations, including monocytes, inflammatory (formerly M1), and regulatory (formerly M2) macrophages and resting mast cells, are all elevated in lesions compared with paired eutopic endometrium.
source: Innate myeloid populations, including monocytes, inflammatory (formerly M1), and regulatory (formerly M2) macrophages and resting mast cells, are all elevated in lesions compared with paired eutopic endometrium, while fewer activated dendritic cells can be found (Zhou et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2023.

claim: Fewer activated dendritic cells can be found in endometriosis lesions compared with paired eutopic endometrium.
source: Innate myeloid populations, including monocytes, inflammatory (formerly M1), and regulatory (formerly M2) macrophages and resting mast cells, are all elevated in lesions compared with paired eutopic endometrium, while fewer activated dendritic cells can be found (Zhou et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2023.

claim: Endometriosis-associated immune cells display altered signalling and antigen-presenting ability.
source: Functionally, endometriosis-associated immune cells display altered signalling (Tan et al., 2022) and antigen-presenting ability (Zhu et al., 2023), which could explain the reduced immunosurveillance and phagocytic activity of these cells in vitro (Lukács et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tan et al., 2022 and Zhu et al., 2023.

claim: There is an increase in resident adaptive lymphocytes such as memory B cells, plasma cells, and both resting and activated CD4+ and CD8+ cells in endometriosis compared to matched eutopic endometrium.
source: Similarly, there is an increase in resident adaptive lymphocytes such as memory B cells, plasma cells, and both resting and activated CD4+ and CD8+ cells, with a reduction in the number of regulatory T-cells and both resting and activated natural killer cells (Zhou et al., 2023; Zhu et al., 2023) in endometriosis compared to matched eutopic endometrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhou et al., 2023 and Zhu et al., 2023.

claim: There is a reduction in the number of regulatory T-cells and both resting and activated natural killer cells in endometriosis compared to matched eutopic endometrium.
source: Similarly, there is an increase in resident adaptive lymphocytes such as memory B cells, plasma cells, and both resting and activated CD4+ and CD8+ cells, with a reduction in the number of regulatory T-cells and both resting and activated natural killer cells (Zhou et al., 2023; Zhu et al., 2023) in endometriosis compared to matched eutopic endometrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhou et al., 2023 and Zhu et al., 2023.

claim: Orchestrated immune dysregulation in endometriosis extends beyond the immediate microenvironment, creating a systemic proinflammatory milieu in favour of a Th2 cytokine response.
source: This orchestrated immune dysregulation extends beyond the immediate microenvironment, creating a systemic proinflammatory milieu in favour of a Th2 cytokine response (Xia et al., 2023; Olkowska-Truchanowicz et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Xia et al., 2023 and Olkowska-Truchanowicz et al., 2021.

claim: Laparoscopy remains the mainstay of endometriosis diagnosis.
source: There remains no simple diagnostic test for endometriosis, and while efforts are being made to improve access and accuracy of imaging, laparoscopy remains the mainstay of endometriosis diagnosis.
evidence: This is stated as current clinical practice.

claim: Treatment options for endometriosis remain limited to surgical, hormonal, or analgesic management.
source: Treatment options remain limited to surgical, hormonal, or analgesic management, and there is a significant unmet clinical need for novel therapies.
evidence: This is stated as current clinical practice.

claim: Diagnosis and prognosis, disease aetiology, and treatment have been identified as the top research priorities by endometriosis patients.
source: These topics – diagnosis and prognosis, disease aetiology, and treatment – have also been identified as the top research priorities by endometriosis patients (Armour et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Armour et al., 2023.

claim: Eutopic endometrium from people with endometriosis demonstrates profound structural, transcriptomic, methylomic, proteomic, and immunologic differences from 'healthy' (control) endometrium.
source: Eutopic endometrium from people with endometriosis demonstrates profound structural, transcriptomic, methylomic, proteomic, and immunologic differences from 'healthy' (control) endometrium (Tan et al., 2022; Adamczyk et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2021; Méar et al., 2022; Prašnikar et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tan et al., 2022, Adamczyk et al., 2022, Wu et al., 2021, Méar et al., 2022, and Prašnikar et al., 2020.

claim: Neural fibre marker PGP 9.5 demonstrated comparable accuracy to traditional surgical diagnosis for endometriosis.
source: Understanding these differences was of significant interest in the development of an endometrial biopsy-based diagnostic test, of which neural fibre marker PGP 9.5 demonstrated comparable accuracy to traditional surgical diagnosis (Gupta et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gupta et al., 2016.

claim: Collecting endometrial fluid directly from the uterine cavity has shown utility in diagnosing endometrioma by lipidomic profiling.
source: Collecting endometrial fluid directly from the uterine cavity has shown utility in diagnosing endometrioma by lipidomic profiling (Domínguez et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Domínguez et al., 2017.

claim: Cytokine profiles in endometrial or cervicovaginal lavage samples, namely IL-1A, IL-6, and RANTES, have shown predictive capacity to identify endometriosis of variable phenotypes versus symptomatic controls.
source: Cytokine profiles in endometrial or cervicovaginal lavage samples, namely IL-1A, IL-6, and Regulated on Activation, Normal T cell Expressed and Secreted (RANTES), have shown predictive capacity to identify endometriosis of variable phenotypes versus symptomatic controls (Llarena et al., 2020; Jimenez et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Llarena et al., 2020 and Jimenez et al., 2024.

claim: Distinct inflammatory signatures were observed between early (I/II) versus late (III/IV) stage, and endometrioma versus peritoneal lesions in endometrial lavage samples.
source: Within endometriosis cases, distinct inflammatory signatures were observed between early (I/II) versus late (III/IV) stage, and endometrioma versus peritoneal lesions (Jimenez et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jimenez et al., 2024.

claim: Exosomes from endometrial lavage have identified a specific microRNA (miRNA), miR-210-3p, as upregulated in those with endometrioma, irrespective of menstrual phase.
source: Exosomes from endometrial lavage have identified a specific microRNA (miRNA), miR-210-3p, as upregulated in those with endometrioma, irrespective of menstrual phase (Jiang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jiang et al., 2022.

claim: MicroRNAs have been successfully isolated from extracellular vesicles collected from both cervical brush samples and vaginal swabs in endometriosis patients.
source: These miRNAs have also been successfully isolated from extracellular vesicles collected from both cervical brush samples and vaginal swabs in endometriosis patients (Paterson et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Paterson et al., 2024.

claim: Menstrual blood is already used for clinical monitoring of glucose control in diabetes via FDA-approved menstrual pad, Q-Pad.
source: Menstrual blood is already used for clinical monitoring of glucose control in diabetes via FDA-approved menstrual pad, Q-Pad (Naseri and Therkelsen, 2021; Naseri and Therkelsen, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Naseri and Therkelsen, 2021 and Naseri and Therkelsen, 2017.

claim: Comparison of eutopic and ectopic tissue somatic mutation burden supports an endometrial origin of endometriosis lesions.
source: Comparison of eutopic and ectopic tissue somatic mutation burden supports an endometrial origin of endometriosis lesions, though the prevalence and clinical significance of this aetiology remain unresolved.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from comparative studies.

claim: An endometrial origin of endometriosis has been observed across all major phenotypes.
source: An endometrial origin of endometriosis has been observed across all major phenotypes (Noë et al., 2018; Li et al., 2021a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Noë et al., 2018 and Li et al., 2021a.

claim: Individual case studies show that disease evolution is unique, with heterogenous cell phylogenies between patients.
source: Individual case studies show that disease evolution is unique, with heterogenous cell phylogenies between patients (Li et al., 2021a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2021a.

claim: Both epithelial and mesenchymal endometriosis cells have been traced to an endometrial origin.
source: Both epithelial (Suda et al., 2018; Li et al., 2014) and mesenchymal (Suda et al., 2019; Noë et al., 2018; Li et al., 2021a) endometriosis cells have been traced to an endometrial origin.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Suda et al., 2018, Li et al., 2014, Suda et al., 2019, Noë et al., 2018, and Li et al., 2021a.

claim: Endometriosis-initiating cells likely represent endometrial stem cells.
source: It is likely that these endometriosis-initiating cells represent endometrial stem cells, with markers of both endometrial epithelial (Tan et al., 2022; Fonseca et al., 2023; Garcia-Alonso et al., 2021; Valentijn et al., 2013; Zeitvogel et al., 2001) and mesenchymal (Tan et al., 2022) stem cells identified in endometriosis tissue.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies identifying stem cell markers.

claim: When isolated from lesions, endometriosis stem cells demonstrate the same colony-forming efficiencies and cellular reprogramming capacities as eutopic endometrial stem cells.
source: When isolated from lesions, endometriosis stem cells demonstrate the same colony-forming efficiencies and cellular reprogramming capacities as eutopic endometrial stem cells, able to differentiate into adipocytes, osteoblasts, chondrocytes, cardiomyocytes, and neural cells (Kao et al., 2011; Li et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kao et al., 2011 and Li et al., 2023.

claim: Endometrium-derived endometriosis-initiating stem cells are theorised to be transported to ectopic sites via retrograde menstruation, iatrogenesis, lymphatic, or haematological spread.
source: It is theorised that these endometrium-derived endometriosis-initiating stem cells are transported to ectopic sites via retrograde menstruation (Masuda et al., 2021), iatrogenesis (Benedetto et al., 2022; Neamtu et al., 2022), lymphatic (Velho et al., 2023; Jerman et al., 2020), or haematological spread (Wang et al., 2024; Kiss et al., 2020; Pospisilova et al., 2019), with case studies supporting each theory.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies supporting different transport mechanisms.

claim: Decreased apoptosis, increased proliferation, and inflammation observed in eutopic endometrium give disease-initiating cells a survival advantage and facilitate their adhesion and invasion of parenchymal tissues.
source: Upon transport to ectopic locations, it is postulated that decreased apoptosis (Prašnikar et al., 2020; Schwalie et al., 2024), increased proliferation (Tan et al., 2022), and inflammation (Tan et al., 2022; Shih et al., 2022) observed in eutopic endometrium give these disease-initiating cells a survival advantage and facilitate their adhesion and invasion of parenchymal tissues such as peritoneum or ovarian epithelium.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies and represents a theoretical model.

claim: Localised progestin treatment via levonorgestrel intrauterine systems (LNG-IUS) has been shown to decrease symptom recurrence.
source: Localised progestin treatment via levonorgestrel intrauterine systems (LNG-IUS) has been shown to decrease symptom recurrence (Kim et al., 2022) and reoperation rates in endometrioma (Choi et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2022.

claim: LNG-IUS has been shown to decrease reoperation rates in endometrioma.
source: Localised progestin treatment via levonorgestrel intrauterine systems (LNG-IUS) has been shown to decrease symptom recurrence (Kim et al., 2022) and reoperation rates in endometrioma (Choi et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Choi et al., 2023.

claim: LNG-IUS use is associated with reduced menstrual bleeding or complete amenorrhea.
source: While LNG-IUS use is associated with reduced menstrual bleeding or complete amenorrhea (Parks et al., 2020), this action is independent of any effect on circulating estradiol (Tasci et al., 2009) and minimal effects on ovulation (Apter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Parks et al., 2020.

claim: LNG-IUS action is independent of any effect on circulating estradiol.
source: While LNG-IUS use is associated with reduced menstrual bleeding or complete amenorrhea (Parks et al., 2020), this action is independent of any effect on circulating estradiol (Tasci et al., 2009) and minimal effects on ovulation (Apter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tasci et al., 2009.

claim: LNG-IUS has minimal effects on ovulation.
source: While LNG-IUS use is associated with reduced menstrual bleeding or complete amenorrhea (Parks et al., 2020), this action is independent of any effect on circulating estradiol (Tasci et al., 2009) and minimal effects on ovulation (Apter et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Apter et al., 2014.

claim: A meta-analysis of RNA expression differences between patient-matched endometriosis and eutopic endometrium found an overall difference of only 4.74% (15,234/321,149 genes).
source: A meta-analysis of RNA expression differences between patient-matched endometriosis and eutopic endometrium found an overall difference of only 4.74% (15,234/321,149 genes) (Riaz et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Riaz et al., 2024.

claim: The overall goal of hormonal agents is to induce a hypoestrogenic state by targeting various points in the hypothalamus–pituitary–ovary axis.
source: For example, the overall goal of hormonal agents is to induce a hypoestrogenic state by targeting various points in the hypothalamus–pituitary–ovary axis (Alonso et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Alonso et al., 2024.

claim: Hypoestrogenic state can benefit endometriosis lesions directly by reducing proliferation and increasing apoptosis.
source: This can benefit endometriosis lesions directly by reducing proliferation and increasing apoptosis (Gomes et al., 2009; Kiba et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gomes et al., 2009 and Kiba et al., 2015.

claim: Hypoestrogenic state decreases endometrial innervation.
source: However, the effects of this hypoestrogenic state extend beyond the endometriotic lesion itself, decreasing endometrial innervation (Tokushige et al., 2008), and overall menstrual volume (Niu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tokushige et al., 2008.

claim: Hypoestrogenic state decreases overall menstrual volume.
source: However, the effects of this hypoestrogenic state extend beyond the endometriotic lesion itself, decreasing endometrial innervation (Tokushige et al., 2008), and overall menstrual volume (Niu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Niu et al., 2021.

claim: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogues can result in vasomotor symptoms and a loss of bone mineral density.
source: This is particularly relevant for second-line agents such as gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogues, which can result in vasomotor symptoms and a loss of bone mineral density (Della Corte et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Della Corte et al., 2020.

claim: Next-generation hormonal agents currently under development are focussing on the known difference in oestrogen metabolism between eutopic and ectopic tissues.
source: In an attempt to increase specificity, next-generation hormonal agents currently under development are focussing on the known difference in oestrogen metabolism between eutopic and ectopic tissues (Mercorio et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mercorio et al., 2022.

claim: PI3K/AKT and MAPK inhibitors have been shown to be more cytotoxic to cells from eutopic endometrium than endometriosis lesions.
source: For instance, despite growing data suggesting that PI3K/AKT and MAPK represent targets of priority for endometriosis treatment (Bao et al., 2022), inhibitors of these pathways have been shown to be more cytotoxic to cells from eutopic endometrium than endometriosis lesions (Lavogina et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lavogina et al., 2019.

claim: Parenchyma and the surrounding local microenvironment is not merely a passive bystander, but an active contributor to endometriosis progression.
source: There is increasing evidence that parenchyma and the surrounding local microenvironment is not merely a passive bystander, but an active contributor to endometriosis progression.
evidence: This is stated as an emerging understanding in the field.

claim: Mesothelial cells are known to be present within endometriosis lesions.
source: Mesothelial cells are known to be present within endometriosis lesions (Kerner et al., 1981) and undergo mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition to promote disease progression and fibrosis (Yan et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kerner et al., 1981.

claim: Mesothelial cells undergo mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition to promote disease progression and fibrosis in endometriosis.
source: Mesothelial cells are known to be present within endometriosis lesions (Kerner et al., 1981) and undergo mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition to promote disease progression and fibrosis (Yan et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yan et al., 2020.

claim: Retroperitoneal adipose tissue from people with endometriosis demonstrate higher amounts of fibrosis, angiogenesis, and immune infiltration than controls, even in areas without lesions of endometriosis.
source: Even in areas without lesions of endometriosis, retroperitoneal adipose tissue from people with endometriosis demonstrate higher amounts of fibrosis, angiogenesis, and immune infiltration than controls, likely mediated by the systemic proinflammatory milieu initiated by disease (Kubo et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kubo et al., 2021.

claim: Surgical translocation of murine endometrium into the peritoneum is sufficient to induce an upregulation of immune, fibrosis, and angiogenesis pathways akin to endometriosis lesions.
source: Microenvironmental cues themselves seem to promote disease progression, with mere surgical translocation of murine endometrium into the peritoneum sufficient to induce an upregulation of immune, fibrosis, and angiogenesis pathways akin to endometriosis lesions (Li et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2024.

claim: Circulating cell-free non-coding RNAs, such as miRNAs and long-non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), are abundant in blood and play important roles in normal inter-cell communication.
source: Circulating cell-free non-coding RNAs, such as miRNAs and long-non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), are abundant in blood and play important roles in normal inter-cell communication (Ramón Y Cajal et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ramón Y Cajal et al., 2019.

claim: Both miRNAs and lncRNAs are dysregulated in endometriosis patients versus controls and have been implicated in disease pathogenesis via their involvement in inflammatory, immune, and hormonal responses.
source: Both miRNAs and lncRNAs are dysregulated in endometriosis patients versus controls and have been implicated in disease pathogenesis via their involvement in inflammatory, immune, and hormonal responses (Hon et al., 2023; Ghafouri-Fard et al., 2020; Abbaszadeh et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hon et al., 2023, Ghafouri-Fard et al., 2020, and Abbaszadeh et al., 2023.

claim: Recent characterisation of the circulating miRNA transcriptome using plasma samples from 153 patients with endometriosis has informed a diagnostic signature of 86 miRNAs in adults of undisclosed phenotype.
source: Recent characterisation of the circulating miRNA transcriptome using plasma samples from 153 patients with endometriosis has informed a diagnostic signature of 86 miRNAs in adults of undisclosed phenotype (Bendifallah et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bendifallah et al., 2022.

claim: The downregulation of lncRNA, LINC01456, in serum is associated with advanced disease stage and is predictive of endometrioma recurrence.
source: Beyond diagnosis, circulating non-coding RNAs may also hold prognostic value. The downregulation of lncRNA, LINC01456, in serum is associated with advanced disease stage and is predictive of endometrioma recurrence (Song et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Song et al., 2024.

claim: Serum miR-1307-3p levels have shown clinical value, predicting the efficacy of perioperative dienogest treatment for ovarian reserve preservation after endometrioma cystectomy.
source: Serum miR-1307-3p levels have also shown clinical value, predicting the efficacy of perioperative dienogest treatment for ovarian reserve preservation after endometrioma cystectomy (Yabuki et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yabuki et al., 2024.

claim: Phenotype-specific differences in cfDNA concentration and fragmentation have been observed in endometriosis.
source: Phenotype-specific differences in cfDNA concentration and fragmentation have been observed (Yuwono et al., 2022; Haouzi et al., 2018), supporting the need for large, unbiased sample cohorts to account for endometriosis heterogeneity.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yuwono et al., 2022 and Haouzi et al., 2018.

claim: Those with endometriosis showed significantly decreased cfDNA fragmentation compared to controls.
source: While those with endometriosis showed significantly decreased cfDNA fragmentation compared to controls (Yuwono et al., 2022), attempts to increase test specificity by investigating cfDNA methylation signatures relied upon endometrial methylation patterns, which have not been investigated in endometriosis tissues (Yuwono et al., 2022; Alonso et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Yuwono et al., 2022.

claim: Attempts to establish an endometriosis diagnostic signature in blood have been more accurate than in menstrual effluent, with higher overall sensitivities and specificities (96.8 vs 87.5 and 100.0 vs 91.7, respectively).
source: To date, attempts to establish an endometriosis diagnostic signature in blood have been more accurate than in menstrual effluent, with higher overall sensitivities and specificities (96.8 vs 87.5 and 100.0 vs 91.7, respectively) (Nayyar et al., 2020; Bendifallah et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nayyar et al., 2020 and Bendifallah et al., 2022.

claim: There have been 47 case reports of endometriosis arising in people with MRKH syndrome.
source: For example, despite the 47 case reports of endometriosis arising in people with MRKH syndrome (Wang et al., 2017; Steinmacher et al., 2022; Marsh et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2022; Mok-Lin et al., 2010; Cho et al., 2009), the majority of patients (45/47, 95.7%) retained uterine remnants, of which all cases which underwent histological review contained functional endometrium (35/35, 100%) (Steinmacher et al., 2022; Marsh et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple case reports.

claim: The majority of patients with MRKH syndrome and endometriosis (45/47, 95.7%) retained uterine remnants.
source: For example, despite the 47 case reports of endometriosis arising in people with MRKH syndrome (Wang et al., 2017; Steinmacher et al., 2022; Marsh et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2022; Mok-Lin et al., 2010; Cho et al., 2009), the majority of patients (45/47, 95.7%) retained uterine remnants, of which all cases which underwent histological review contained functional endometrium (35/35, 100%) (Steinmacher et al., 2022; Marsh et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a finding from the review of case reports.

claim: All cases of MRKH syndrome with endometriosis which underwent histological review contained functional endometrium (35/35, 100%).
source: For example, despite the 47 case reports of endometriosis arising in people with MRKH syndrome (Wang et al., 2017; Steinmacher et al., 2022; Marsh et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2022; Mok-Lin et al., 2010; Cho et al., 2009), the majority of patients (45/47, 95.7%) retained uterine remnants, of which all cases which underwent histological review contained functional endometrium (35/35, 100%) (Steinmacher et al., 2022; Marsh et al., 2013; Tian et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a finding from the review of case reports with histological review.

claim: Only two isolated cases of endometriosis have been reported in the context of complete uterine agenesis: one endometrioma and one peritoneal endometriosis.
source: In fact, only two isolated cases of endometriosis have been reported in the context of complete uterine agenesis: one endometrioma (Cho et al., 2009) and one peritoneal endometriosis (Mok-Lin et al., 2010), the latter of which was not histologically confirmed due to lesion ablation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cho et al., 2009 and Mok-Lin et al., 2010.

claim: There have been 24 case reports of endometriosis in cisgender men and one case in a transgender woman.
source: Similarly, despite 24 case reports of endometriosis in cisgender men and one case in a transgender woman (Coleman-Belin et al., 2024), at least four of these patients presented with innate variations of sex (intersex) characteristics (Nerune et al., 2016; Vaughn and Gonzalez-angulo, 1961; Patel and Doody, 2008; Ohan et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Coleman-Belin et al., 2024.

claim: At least four patients with endometriosis in cisgender men presented with innate variations of sex (intersex) characteristics.
source: Similarly, despite 24 case reports of endometriosis in cisgender men and one case in a transgender woman (Coleman-Belin et al., 2024), at least four of these patients presented with innate variations of sex (intersex) characteristics (Nerune et al., 2016; Vaughn and Gonzalez-angulo, 1961; Patel and Doody, 2008; Ohan et al., 2024).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nerune et al., 2016, Vaughn and Gonzalez-angulo, 1961, Patel and Doody, 2008, and Ohan et al., 2024.

claim: A histological review of 110 endometriomas revealed 34 cases with areas of direct transition from normal native epithelium to endometriosis.
source: A histological review of 110 endometriomas revealed 34 cases with areas of direct transition from normal native epithelium to endometriosis (Zheng et al., 2005), an observation that is yet to be recorded in either superficial or deep infiltrating peritoneal lesions.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zheng et al., 2005.

claim: All observed cases of endometriosis in non-primate (and therefore non-menstruating) animals have presented as endometriomas (5/5 dogs, 1/1 guinea pigs).
source: Interestingly, all observed cases of endometriosis in non-primate (and therefore non-menstruating) animals have also presented as endometriomas (5/5 dogs, 1/1 guinea pigs), which may further support that endometriomas are more likely to develop independently of endometrium than other phenotypes of endometriosis (Demirel, 2017; Paiva et al., 2015; Baldi et al., 2017; Bartel et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Demirel, 2017, Paiva et al., 2015, Baldi et al., 2017, and Bartel et al., 2011.

claim: Evidence of clonal metastasis from endometrioma to peritoneal locations indicates that the development of diverse phenotypes could arise from a single initiating event.
source: However, evidence of clonal metastasis from endometrioma to peritoneal locations indicates that the development of diverse phenotypes could arise from a single initiating event, which cannot, at this stage, exclude metaplasia (Praetorius et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Praetorius et al., 2022.

claim: In cancer, transcriptional profiles of 'normal' tumour-adjacent tissue have been found to have prognostic value.
source: For example, in cancer, transcriptional profiles of 'normal' tumour-adjacent tissue have been found to have prognostic value (Kim et al., 2023; Oh and Lee, 2023), and there are increasing efforts to target native microenvironment fibrosis, neovascularisation, and inflammation to improve patient outcomes (Xiao and Yu, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2023 and Oh and Lee, 2023.

claim: In Crohn's disease, adjacent mesenteric adipose tissue actively contributes to disease development and fibrosis.
source: In Crohn's disease, adjacent mesenteric adipose tissue actively contributes to disease development and fibrosis (Huang et al., 2022), and may have a direct effect on the efficacy of infliximab treatment (Shen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2022.

claim: Adjacent mesenteric adipose tissue in Crohn's disease may have a direct effect on the efficacy of infliximab treatment.
source: In Crohn's disease, adjacent mesenteric adipose tissue actively contributes to disease development and fibrosis (Huang et al., 2022), and may have a direct effect on the efficacy of infliximab treatment (Shen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shen et al., 2018.

claim: Clinical trials targeting resident synovial fibroblasts are currently underway in rheumatoid arthritis.
source: Clinical trials targeting resident synovial fibroblasts are currently underway in rheumatoid arthritis (Siebert et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Siebert et al., 2020.

claim: There is evidence supporting both endometrial-dependent and endometrial-independent pathogenesis of endometriosis.
source: With evidence supporting both endometrial-dependent (Suda et al., 2018) and endometrial-independent pathogenesis (Zheng et al., 2005), neither theory provides sufficient evidence to preclude the other, and they likely represent separate aetiological avenues of distinct subtypes of endometriosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Suda et al., 2018 and Zheng et al., 2005.

claim: Endometrial-dependent and endometrial-independent pathogenesis likely represent separate aetiological avenues of distinct subtypes of endometriosis.
source: With evidence supporting both endometrial-dependent (Suda et al., 2018) and endometrial-independent pathogenesis (Zheng et al., 2005), neither theory provides sufficient evidence to preclude the other, and they likely represent separate aetiological avenues of distinct subtypes of endometriosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the evidence presented.

claim: The current analysis likely does not account for every dataset generated for endometriosis research and cannot report on data generated but not publicly shared.
source: The current analysis likely does not account for every dataset generated for endometriosis research and cannot report on data generated but not publicly shared.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors.

claim: There was a sizeable overlap of available data on both GEO and ArrayExpress sites (75/245, 30.20%).
source: However, by analysing the publicly available data from two of the most popular sites for data sharing, this review found a sizeable overlap of available data on both sites (75/245, 30.20%), indicating that there was a moderate saturation and that the main findings of this analysis represent a true bias in field towards endometrium-derived data in endometriosis research.
evidence: This is a finding from the dataset analysis.

claim: The number of biospecimens relying solely on endometrium published each year consistently remains approximately 50%.
source: Despite an increasing understanding in recent years of the innate biological differences between endometriosis and endometrium, the number of biospecimens relying solely on endometrium published each year consistently remains approximately 50% (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C and represents a temporal analysis finding.

claim: The lack of temporal shift towards more inclusive sampling is indicative of a persistent bias in the field of both thought and methodology.
source: The lack of temporal shift towards more inclusive sampling is indicative of a persistent bias in the field of both thought and methodology.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal analysis of datasets.

claim: The perception that endometriosis tissue represents 'ectopic endometrium' is a fundamentally flawed and outdated concept.
source: The perception that endometriosis tissue represents 'ectopic endometrium' is a fundamentally flawed and outdated concept, and an overall misnomer.
evidence: This is the central thesis of the manuscript.

claim: The clinical definition of endometriosis currently remains hinged upon endometrium, with histopathological diagnostic criteria dependent on the identification of endometrium-like glandular epithelium admixed with stromal cells.
source: Nevertheless, the clinical definition of endometriosis currently remains hinged upon endometrium, with histopathological diagnostic criteria dependent on the identification of endometrium-like glandular epithelium admixed with stromal cells.
evidence: This describes the current clinical definition.
